findings.note: The only security review on record does not cover the shipped runner. Its header names the reviewed artifact as specs/epic-194-a6-lite-integration/drafts/apply-protected-files.ps1, which was deleted on promotion with no digest of the reviewed bytes recorded; the document's own addendum states 'the 2026-08-08 PASS should be read as scoped to a predecessor artifact, not to what ships' and lists three post-review commits that touch boundaries it assessed (9997091c four-to-five-target widening, 75fe25a3 SourceMode rewrite, 2499e813 typed catch split). It also records the shipped runner as sha256 15417bd5ef2d5bad46e8b9800d9d27a17a8df6c3fc578bfa3de57b49ab3688a8 and says a PASS over the current bytes 'requires a fresh independent security pass'. T-001 is Risk: high / Security-Sensitive: true and its Done-When explicitly requires this runner be security-reviewed before it is used to apply T-002/T-003's real protected-file payload; that item is unsatisfied for the bytes actually delivered.

Two REQUIRED checks in the task's own default-FAIL verification contract are recorded passes:false. (1) 'regression' — the evidence log (verification/qg/shared/regression.log) states the full tests/run-all.sh (116 suites) TIMED OUT after 10 minutes mid-run and was never completed; the contract itself says this 'makes the contract fail overall on this required check, which is the correct outcome until tests/run-all.sh is actually run to completion in one session'. (2) 'placeholder-scan' — the named log ends 'Placeholder scan FAILED (5 finding(s)) ... exit: 1' against CHANGELOG.md, a declared Output of this task, and the contract records that the scanner's only exemption is explicit human acceptance in a quality-gate report, of which none exists for this feature ('verification/qg/ holds logs only'). A contract failing two required checks cannot support a clean acceptance of T-001.

The Outputs table claims 'every hash below is the file's current on-disk value' (re-derived 2026-08-25), but the bundle marks 8 of the 15 declared paths as changed since the report was written (CHANGELOG.md, tests/human-copy-runner-contract.tests.ps1, human-copy/apply-protected-files.ps1, human-copy/MANIFEST.sha256, and all four staged plugins/sdd-lite payloads). The report's explicit completeness claim — 'The five staged payload digests above are exactly the five lines of MANIFEST.sha256; shasum -a 256 -c MANIFEST.sha256 run from the human-copy/ root reports OK for all five' — is contradicted by the MANIFEST.sha256 carried in this same bundle: four of the five digests differ (check-risk-upgrade.sh declared ee35d426..., manifest 4ffd5cd7...; check-risk-upgrade.ps1 6be23a33... vs f627ab50...; risk-upgrade-policy.md dab10b8b... vs 40103332...; lite-spec/SKILL.md 798ed3fb... vs 52d428aa...), only .github/workflows/test.yml (dc0cc24c...) agreeing. The runner is likewise declared 8fc01f58... while security-review.md records the shipped runner as 15417bd5.... For a task whose entire deliverable is hash-verified integrity, the declared-Outputs record is not trustworthy as written.

findings.ref: reports/implementation/epic-194-a6-lite-integration/T-001.md ('Four-target / fifth-target contradiction (unchanged from the prior resume's own recommendation)')
findings.note: This section is stale and directly contradicts the shipped artifacts, the feature README, and the report's own later text. It asserts 'MANIFEST.sha256 and $Script:DeclaredTargets stay at exactly four entries' and instructs that .github/workflows/test.yml 'is applied by a plain, human-reviewed cp (never through the runner) and must be removed from human-copy/ before the runner is ever invoked'. The delivered runner declares five targets, MANIFEST.sha256 carries five entries, and requirements.md AC-010/AC-031 (as amended 2026-08-21) require the fifth target to be applied through the runner's exact-set/hash/post-copy envelope, 'never a bare cp'. An operator acting on this section would bypass exactly the control AC-031 and design.md's STRIDE row B5 exist to enforce, and would also break TEST-000d, which hard-fails when the staged workflow candidate is absent — the same mutually-exclusive-preconditions defect a prior panel raised against the now-deleted human-copy/README.md.

The operator-facing verification table lists ee35d426... / 6be23a33... / dab10b8b... / 798ed3fb... for the four plugins/sdd-lite staged targets, which disagree with MANIFEST.sha256's current entries for those same paths (4ffd5cd7... / f627ab50... / 40103332... / 52d428aa...); only the fifth row (.github/workflows/test.yml, dc0cc24c...) agrees. This README is the document the Human-apply command sequence lives in for a Risk: high, Security-Sensitive protected-file application. Either the table is stale against the staged payload, or MANIFEST.sha256 is — in the latter case Test-ManifestHashes rejects the batch and it cannot be applied at all. Either way the delivered records of the same five digests do not agree with each other.

The contract pins spec_revision 2740928c9e9c45cd56644a0e22e4fb5fc3c270932eba9c8fecf4a8450780d437 while its own comment discloses that this value predates the 2026-08-21 AC-010 amendment (9997091c) and that the current value is 466465e04248cb912635ed83435ff0c17e9805648e0caead7132ad6276a34d23. The contract therefore certifies a specification revision other than the one under review. The disclosure and the named owner for the re-issue (the next quality-gate run) are appropriate; the stale pin still stands unresolved.

The implementation report's TDD/Done-When self-check, verification/T-001/validation-summary.md, and the contract's own comment all assert 45/45 on both runtimes, while the current green captures (verification/T-001.green.log and verification/qg/T-001/unit-acceptance-green.log, both recaptured 2026-08-25 against HEAD 4905c131) record 56/56. The 45-assertion captures at verification/T-001/green-sh.log and green-ps1.log remain in the verification directory alongside the 56-assertion ones with nothing stating which is current, so a reader cannot tell from the evidence set which run the narrative describes.

The assertions are correct — Test-AllLiveFilesOriginal iterates all five entries of $DeclaredTargets (sourced from tests/fixtures/epic-194-human-copy/scenarios.json, which declares five) — but their emitted text still reads 'all four live files unchanged' / 'all four live targets remain unchanged', and TEST-002's banner still calls the extra path an 'undeclared fifth' when it is now a sixth. These strings are what a reviewer sees verbatim in the GREEN evidence logs, where they understate the scope actually checked.

T-001's Done-When requires 'CHANGELOG.md gains a NEW ## Unreleased entry citing #194'. The delivered file's head runs '# Changelog' directly into '## v1.17.0 (2026-08-27)' with no ## Unreleased section, so that Done-When item is not verifiable against the current file (the bundle elides the middle of the file, so the #194 text itself cannot be located either). The entry appears to have been absorbed by the v1.17.0 release; the checkbox as written no longer describes an observable state.

findings.note: The Windows half of the publisher (NtCreateFile / SetFileInformationByHandle / RtlNtStatusToDosError P/Invoke, the handle-relative rename, and reparse-point validation) has been reviewed statically and never executed; the review states 'No log in this feature's evidence shows it executing.' For a high-risk protected-file publisher shipped as a PowerShell-native tool on a cross-platform repository, one of the two supported runtimes has no execution evidence at all behind its path-safety and atomic-publish claims.
